name: AFib Amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Hereditary Fibrinogen A Alpha-Chain Amyloidosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in the fibrinogen A alpha-chain gene (FGA)
Amyloid deposits confirmed by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence on biopsy
Evidence of renal amyloid deposition causing proteinuria or renal impairment
Positive family history of amyloidosis or renal disease
Amyloid typing by mass spectrometry confirming fibrinogen A alpha-chain composition

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic FGA mutation plus histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with organ involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires genetic and histopathological confirmation due to overlap with other amyloidoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Renal amyloid deposition with nephrotic syndrome
searchTerms: protein loss in urine from amyloid in kidneys

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid fibril deposits in glomeruli confirmed by biopsy

searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues

common.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly due to amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: mild hepatomegaly caused by protein deposits

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema related to nephrotic syndrome
searchTerms: swelling in limbs from kidney disease
fluid retention due to nephrotic syndrome
peripheral swelling related to kidney problems

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and urea indicating renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or enlarged kidneys
Echocardiogram may show mild ventricular thickening
other: Congo red staining of biopsy specimens with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Amyloid typing by laser microdissection and mass spectrometry

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
More frequent cardiac involvement with restrictive cardiomyopathy
Predominant involvement of kidneys and liver without FGA mutations

redFlags: Family history of amyloidosis or unexplained renal disease
references: Sipe JD, Benson MD, Buxbaum JN, et al. Nomenclature 2014: Amyloid fibril proteins and clinical classification of the amyloidosis. Amyloid. 2014;21(4):221-224.
